course.title: Express js
course.description: A complete Express 5 course from first server to production-oriented API architecture. Students learn the middleware and routing model, HTTP request/response handling, modular routers, validation, error handling, browser boundaries, sessions, security, persistence architecture, testing, performance, reverse-proxy deployment, health checks, graceful shutdown, API resilience, and a realistic final service.
prerequisites: JavaScript fundamentals including functions, objects, modules, promises, and async/await.
Basic HTTP concepts: methods, status codes, headers, URLs, and JSON.
learningOutcomes: Build Express 5 applications with deliberate middleware and routing architecture.
Design modular APIs with validation, versioning, pagination, and stable error contracts.
Implement centralized error handling and Express 5 async failure propagation.
Apply security controls for CORS, cookies, sessions, Helmet, redirects, authentication, authorization, and input boundaries.
Separate HTTP, domain, and persistence concerns.
Test real HTTP contracts and reusable middleware.
Improve performance with asynchronous I/O, compression, caching, timeouts, and bounded work.
Prepare services for reverse proxies, health checks, graceful shutdown, and multi-instance deployment.
Complete and explain a production-oriented Express service.

code.src/middleware/validateTicket.js:
import { AppError } from "../errors/AppError.js";
export function validateTicket(req,res,next){const title=typeof req.body?.title==="string"?req.body.title.trim():"";const description=typeof req.body?.description==="string"?req.body.description.trim():"";const priority=req.body?.priority??"normal";if(!title||title.length>120)return next(new AppError(400,"invalid_title","title must be 1-120 characters"));if(description.length>2000)return next(new AppError(400,"invalid_description","description is too long"));if(!["low","normal","high"].includes(priority))return next(new AppError(400,"invalid_priority","priority is invalid"));req.validatedTicket={title,description,priority};next();}
code.src/repositories/ticketRepository.js: const tickets=new Map();let nextId=1;export const ticketRepository={async list({page,limit}){const all=[...tickets.values()];return{items:all.slice((page-1)*limit,page*limit),total:all.length};},async findById(id){return tickets.get(id)??null;},async create(input){const now=new Date().toISOString();const t={id:String(nextId++),...input,status:"open",createdAt:now,updatedAt:now};tickets.set(t.id,t);return t;},async updateStatus(id,status){const t=tickets.get(id);if(!t)return null;const u={...t,status,updatedAt:new Date().toISOString()};tickets.set(id,u);return u;}};

project.explanation: The project keeps HTTP composition, process lifecycle, validation, domain behavior, and persistence responsibilities separate. The in-memory repository is intentionally self-contained; a production system would replace it with a real database adapter. The API demonstrates Express 5 promise-aware handlers, security middleware, bounded input, stable errors, observability, operational endpoints, and graceful process shutdown.
